title: Fluorescence in three species of ariophantid land snails from Thailand
content:
ABSTRACT
In molluscs, fluorescence is known to occur in chitons, bivalves, cephalopods, sea slugs and gastropods. Herein, we report fluorescence in three land snails from the family Ariophantidae (Sarika costabilis, Macrochlamys coleus and Macrochlamys tanymentula), all of which exhibit a blue-green fluorescence with a peak emission wavelength (λmax) of 499–514 nm under irradiated UV light (about 365 nm). The fluorescence in S. costabilis is located in the soft body and mucus, while the green fluorescence of the two Macrochlamys species is restricted to the mucus only. The fluorescence of these three snails was compared, in terms of wavelength and anatomical distribution, to other fluorescent molluscs. The fluorescent compounds from S. costabilis were extracted in both Tris-HCl buffer and ethanol with a fluorescent λmax of 492 and 504 nm, respectively. These peaks of fluorescence did not match that of riboflavin, which is one of the compounds often associated with fluorescence in molluscs. This suggests the presence of different fluorescent compounds across species within Mollusca. A wide variety of fluorescence from blue to red has been recorded in molluscs, suggesting that fluorescence has widely diversified colours.
